headline: ECB CONFIRMS HISTORY: Gold Overtakes U.S. Treasuries as World's #1 Reserve Asset — Now 27% of Global Central Bank Holdings
snippet: The European Central Bank's annual report on the euro's international role confirmed gold now accounts for 27% of global central bank reserves, surpassing U.S. Treasuries at 22% for the first time in modern history. ECB President Lagarde cited geopolitical tensions as the primary driver, noting the shift accelerated after Washington froze Russia's dollar reserves in 2022 — with stablecoin issuer Tether emerging as the single largest buyer in 2025 at over 100 tonnes.

headline: COPPER AT $13,800 ALL-TIME HIGH: Goldman Raises Year-End Target — Grasberg and Kamoa-Kakula Restarts Delayed to 2028
snippet: Goldman Sachs raised its 2026 year-end copper target to $13,735/tonne after cutting mine supply forecasts by 350,000 tonnes on disruptions at Grasberg and Kamoa-Kakula, now delayed to 2028. Citigroup targets $15,000/tonne within 12 months. Copper hit a record $14,153 in mid-May and is trading near those levels as U.S. stockpiling has created an estimated 640,000-tonne deficit in the ex-U.S. market.

headline: GOLD DROPS TO $4,448: JOLTS Data Crushes Rate-Cut Hopes — Metal Fails to Reclaim $4,500 All Week
snippet: Gold fell to $4,448/oz on June 3 after U.S. JOLTS data showed job openings surging to near two-year highs, reinforcing expectations the Federal Reserve will keep rates elevated. The metal has struggled to reclaim $4,500 all week; seasonal analysis suggests a June–July demand lull as jewelry fabricator buying typically softens, with the monthly range forecast at $4,300–$4,725.

headline: 27.7m at 166 g/t SILVER: Brixton Metals Confirms Kilogram-Plus Results Across Cobalt Ontario's Langis Camp (TSXV: BBB)
snippet: Brixton Metals (TSXV: BBB) drilled 27.7m at 166.45 g/t Ag — including a 2.3m high-grade core at 1,811 g/t Ag — at the Langis Silver Project in Ontario's historic Cobalt camp. The 2026 campaign is the project's largest ever at 60,000m, targeting both infill and expansion; CEO Gary Thompson says results confirm 'kilogram-per-tonne-plus silver over meaningful widths' between previously reported ultra-high-grade intercepts.

headline: NEW VEIN FOUND: Bunker Hill Mining Expands High-Grade Silver-Lead Cate-8 Discovery at Idaho's Historic Mine (TSX: BNKR)
snippet: Bunker Hill Mining (TSX: BNKR) reported seven drill holes expanding the newly discovered Cate-8 silver-lead vein in the upper levels of Idaho's historic Bunker Hill mine, with consistent siderite-galena intersections from 1–6 feet. Management says the grade consistency and geometry indicate a genuine new discovery that could be incorporated into an early stage of the mine plan.

headline: EAST-WEST GOLD SHIFT: Hong Kong Plans 10x Storage Expansion — 200 to 2,000 Tonnes as Trade Route Rewires
snippet: Hong Kong officials have announced plans to expand the city's gold storage capacity from 200 to over 2,000 tonnes within three years as it cements its role as an East-West gold trading hub. The Hong Kong Gold Clearing House launched operations in May, and Money Metals notes the buildout reflects China's broader strategy of routing physical gold flows through Asian infrastructure and away from London.

headline: FORT KNOX UNDER SCRUTINY: Trump Demands Physical Audit After Ex-CIA Officer Arrested With 300 Gold Bars Worth $40M
snippet: President Trump posted a call to 'physically audit Fort Knox' on Truth Social after federal agents arrested former senior CIA officer David Rush and seized roughly 300 gold bars worth $40 million from his home. The Sound Money Defense League is urging Congress to pass the Gold Reserve Transparency Act, noting U.S. government inspections have historically fallen short of audit standards, with documented instances of broken vault seals and un-re-audited gold movements.

headline: CENTRAL BANKS STILL BUYING: Net 20 Tonnes Added in May — 95% of Bankers Expect Gold Reserves to Keep Growing
snippet: U.S. Global Investors' weekly Gold SWOT reports global central banks bought a net 20 tonnes of gold in May — slightly below the 12-month average of 27 tonnes — while 95% of central bankers surveyed expect official gold reserves to increase. A record 43% plan to add gold in the next 12 months; Ghana's central bank also enacted its 30% gold purchase mandate from large-scale domestic miners on June 1, up from 20%, targeting 157 total reserve tonnes by 2028.

headline: JUNE GOLD OUTLOOK: Experts See $4,400–$4,800 Range — Seasonal Softness Expected Before Later-Month Recovery
snippet: Analysts polled for June see gold range-bound between $4,300–$4,800, with seasonal weakness typical in June–July as jewelry fabricator demand softens. Ridgemont Metals CEO Deric Ned expects a later-month recovery, while Thomas Winmill forecasts a 0–5% decline from current levels. Silver stands at $74/oz with the metal showing stronger industrial demand fundamentals than gold's current technicals suggest.

headline: RARE EARTH CRUNCH: China Approving Under 25% of European Export License Applications — 90% of Processing Stays in Beijing's Control
snippet: China's updated rare earth export licensing regime is approving fewer than 25% of applications from European firms, with sixfold price spikes already recorded for restricted elements. Beijing controls over 90% of global rare earth processing; a temporary suspension of Wave 2 export controls runs until November 2026, after which five additional rare earth elements could return to full restriction simultaneously.

headline: URANIUM WATCH: UEC to Report Fiscal Q3 Results June 9 — Spot Price at $85/lb After Retreating from $101 January High
snippet: Uranium Energy Corp (NYSE: UEC) will release its fiscal Q3 2026 results before markets open on June 9. Uranium spot prices have softened to around $85/lb from the $101/lb peak reached in January as utility contracting has slowed from its prior pace, though the AI-driven power demand thesis and approved construction licences — including Denison Mines' Wheeler River ISR project in Saskatchewan — continue to underpin long-term sector sentiment.
